title: Journey 1: Foundations: from a question to data
subject: statistics
basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation
context: Statistics starts before the first calculation: define the population, the sample, the variable type and the branch of analysis. This journey builds the vocabulary the other eight journeys depend on.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: Journey 2: Describe the data you actually have
subject: statistics
basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation
context: Mean, median and mode answer different questions; variance, standard deviation and IQR measure different units. The visual layer lets you move one point and watch resistance and sensitivity diverge.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: Journey 3: Probability: the space of what could happen
subject: statistics
basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation
context: Probability is a measure over a sample space, not a feeling about a sentence. The lab makes complements, intersections, conditional probability, independence and mutual exclusivity visible in the same space.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: Journey 4: Distributions: shapes with rules
subject: statistics
basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation
context: Binomial counts successes in fixed independent trials; Poisson counts events in a fixed interval; the normal describes a continuous symmetric bell. Each has a different support, parameter meaning and probability rule.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: Journey 5: Sampling and estimation: from one sample to a range
subject: statistics
basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation
context: The central limit theorem is about the distribution of sample means, not about individual observations becoming normal. Standard error and confidence intervals turn that sampling distribution into a calibrated statement.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: Journey 6: Hypothesis testing: evidence under a null model
subject: statistics
basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation
context: A test compares an observed statistic with the distribution it would have under H₀. The p-value is a tail area conditional on that model; α is chosen before the data; failing to reject is not accepting.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: Journey 7: Experimental design: earning a causal claim
subject: statistics
basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation
context: Randomization, control, blinding and a pre-specified outcome are the design features that make groups comparable. The A/B test is one randomized design, not the definition of all experiments.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: Journey 8: Relationships and causality: what r can and cannot say
subject: statistics
basis: Metadata/title rule; organizational placement, not scientific validation
context: Pearson r measures the strength and direction of a linear association. It is not a slope, it can be near zero under a strong curve, and observational co-movement is not a causal effect.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

subject: statistics
basis: Broad subject placement; finer editorial mapping pending

title: 1. The big picture: what is statistics?
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “A statistic is the same thing as a parameter.” A statistic is computed from a sample and varies; a parameter describes the population and is usually unknown.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 2. Data types and what they permit
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “If it is written with digits, it is numerical.” Customer IDs and phone numbers are labels; averaging them is meaningless.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 3. Descriptive vs inferential statistics
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “A sample summary is already a conclusion about the population.” Description stops at the data; inference adds a model, uncertainty and assumptions.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 4. Measures of center
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “The mean is always the best centre.” In a skewed distribution or with outliers, the mean is pulled toward the tail and may stop representing a typical value.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 5. Measures of spread
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “Standard deviation and standard error are interchangeable.” SD describes individual values; SE describes how a statistic varies across repeated samples.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 6. Probability, complements, independence and conditionals
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “Independent means the events cannot happen together.” Independence is about information: knowing B does not change P(A). Mutually exclusive events cannot occur together at all.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 7. Probability distributions: mass vs density
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “The height of the normal curve is the probability of that value.” Height is density; probability is area under the curve between two values.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 8. The binomial distribution
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “Binomial counts how many trials happen.” It counts successes among a fixed number of trials; the number of trials is an input, not the outcome.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 9. The normal distribution and z-scores
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “Changing σ changes the total probability.” The total area stays 1; a larger σ flattens and widens the curve.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 10. The Poisson distribution
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “λ=20 means P(X=20) is high, so 20 is the mode.” λ is a mean count; at integer λ the mode is actually the pair λ−1 and λ.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 11. The central limit theorem
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “The CLT says the data become normal once n is large.” It is the sampling distribution of the mean that approaches normality, not the population or a single sample.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 12. Sampling distribution
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “A sampling distribution is just a bigger sample.” It is the distribution of a statistic over repeated samples — a different object with a different axis.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 13. Standard error
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “SE is the SD of the data divided by √n because the data got narrower.” The data distribution did not change; the sampling distribution of the mean did.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 14. Confidence intervals
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “There is a 95% probability that the fixed parameter is inside this interval.” Once computed, the interval either covers the fixed parameter or does not; 95% is the long-run coverage of the method.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 15. Hypothesis testing and the two hypotheses
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “The test calculates the probability that H₀ is true.” It calculates the probability of data at least this extreme assuming H₀ is true.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 16. The hypothesis-testing workflow
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “The workflow starts with a p-value.” It starts with the question, the populations and the hypotheses; the statistic comes later.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 17. Sampling variability inside a test
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “A difference between sample means proves a difference between populations.” Samples vary; the test asks whether the observed difference is unusual under H₀.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 18. Test statistic and standard error
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “A test statistic of 3.6 is a 3.6% probability.” It is a distance in SE units; the probability comes from the null distribution, not from the number itself.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 19. The p-value
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “The p-value is the overlap between the null and alternative curves.” It is a tail area of the null sampling distribution, not an overlap.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 20. The significance level α
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “α is the probability that the result is wrong.” α is the long-run false-positive rate under H₀ for the chosen rule.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 21. The decision rule
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “Failing to reject proves H₀.” Absence of sufficient evidence against H₀ is not evidence that H₀ is exactly true.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 22. Type I and Type II errors
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “Type I and Type II errors are complements.” They are conditional on different states of reality; α + β is not 1 in general.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 23. Statistical vs practical significance
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “Statistically significant means important.” Significance is about compatibility with H₀; importance depends on effect size, context and cost.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 24. Experiments
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “Any comparison is an experiment.” Without manipulation and a design that controls alternatives, it is an observational comparison.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 25. Controlled experiments
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “Control means do nothing.” A control can receive a placebo or the current standard, and the point is a comparable reference.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 26. Randomization
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “Randomization guarantees the groups are balanced.” It balances in expectation; any one run can still be imbalanced.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 27. Blinding and placebo
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “Double-blind means the analyst also does not know the hypothesis.” It means participants and the people administering or assessing treatment do not know assignment.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 28. RCT vs A/B testing
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “A/B testing and RCTs are unrelated.” An A/B test is a randomized controlled experiment applied to a product change.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 29. Independent and dependent variables
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “Whatever is on the X axis causes the Y.” Axis placement is a convention; only the design supports a causal reading.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 30. Correlation and Pearson r
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “r is the slope.” r is standardized covariance; the slope depends on the units of X and Y and is not bounded by 1.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 31. Pearson correlation and linear relationships
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “r ≈ 0 means no relationship.” It means no *linear* relationship; a U-shape or cycle can be strongly dependent.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 32. Correlation is not causation
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “A high r proves X causes Y.” Association is compatible with reverse causation, confounding and coincidence.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 33. Confounding variables
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “If the correlation is strong, a confounder cannot explain it.” A strong pooled association can be entirely produced or reversed by a third variable.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 34. Correlation vs experiment
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “A correlation study can establish causality if the sample is big enough.” Sample size narrows uncertainty; it does not remove confounding.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 35. Correlation vs regression
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “r=0.8 means Y rises 0.8 units per unit of X.” That is a slope statement; r has no units.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 36. How the topics connect
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “The topics are independent chapters.” Each later method depends on the sampling and probability ideas built earlier.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 37. The formula index
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “The formula is the method.” A formula without its assumptions and data requirements is not a valid analysis.
status: Existing published surface; review labels remain at source

title: 38. Decision rules: when the question changes
subject: statistics
basis: Existing editorial journey metadata
context: “The most advanced method is the safest.” The right method is the one whose assumptions the data and design can support.

title: Internal/external shortcuts and caching
subject: fabric
basis: Content-context review: distinguish the named access/movement/table-state decision within the Lakehouse source.

Internal shortcuts can share Files and Delta Tables. External sources include ADLS, S3, S3-compatible storage, GCS, Dataverse, and supported Iceberg integrations; format and placement still determine consumption. Workspace caching serves eligible external reads from cached content, reducing repeat remote requests. title: Delta files, transaction logs, and controlled changes
subject: fabric
basis: Content-context review: distinguish the named access/movement/table-state decision within the Lakehouse source.
context: Delta adds transaction metadata to columnar Parquet data. The committed log defines which files comprise a snapshot, rather than every physical file being current data. Appends write files and publish a transaction. Updates/deletes/merges can leave historical physical files even when the latest snapshot no longer includes their rows. ACID preserves consistency; optimistic write conflicts can still occur. Time travel reads earlier snapshots while schema evolution permits controlled structural changes. Neither is a promise to keep unlimited history or silently accept every incoming schema.
status: Existing note; open resources and choose the named pack/section

title: VACUUM, OPTIMIZE, and V-Order have different goals
subject: fabric
basis: Content-context review: distinguish the named access/movement/table-state decision within the Lakehouse source.
context: VACUUM physically removes eligible obsolete data files outside the retention threshold. Its main goal is storage cleanup. It does not compact active files, reconstruct deleted historical data, or delete the Delta log as its ordinary purpose. OPTIMIZE compacts active small files. V-Order optimizes Parquet layout at writing or rewriting time for read-heavy consumption, with workload-dependent write overhead. Recovery requires sufficient retained logs AND files. Inspect cleanup candidates and concurrent-reader requirements before deletion; a seven-day retention setting is not a guaranteed seven-day recovery SLA.
status: Existing note; open resources and choose the named pack/section

title: Partition hierarchy, pruning, and cardinality
subject: fabric
basis: Content-context review: distinguish the named access/movement/table-state decision within the Lakehouse source.
context: Hive-style partitioning places data into directories for populated value combinations of one or more keys. The logical row set is unchanged. Usable predicates on partition keys can skip directories. A key with many distinct values, or too many combined keys, can create tiny partitions and frequent small-file writes. Estimate volume per populated partition and align the layout with real predicates or writer boundaries. A tiny teaching table is intentionally unsuitable as a production partitioning example.
